clue.text: Battle to make the cake stay too long in the oven

parts.note: a bannock is a flat Scottish oatmeal cake

parts.words: stay too long in the oven
parts.note: food left too long in the oven will burn

explanation.surface: Instructions for a cake that must be left baking far too long.
explanation.walkthrough: BANNOCKBURN (1314) was Robert the Bruce's victory over the English in Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Bannockburn was a famous Scottish victory over Edward II in 1314, so it names a battle.

clue.text: A method which is useless for the home?

parts.note: a way of doing something is a method

explanation.surface: A technique that turns out to be no good around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: In sport, the away side plays at the other team's ground, so it is no use to the home team; the question mark flags the stretch.
explanation.definitionFit: An away fixture is played at the opponents' ground, the reverse of playing at home.

clue.text: Girl of seven

indicators.note: of here means a part taken out of the other entry, so the rest of its letters are dropped

parts.note: seven refers to the answer at 7 down in this grid

explanation.surface: A girl aged seven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seven' is not a number but the entry 7 down, whose wordplay puts the girl's name inside CREATED; take CREATED away and she is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Nell is a girl's name, short for Eleanor or Helen.

clue.text: Makes free with king at heart

clue.text: A little advertisement forbids praise being distributed although they are gorgeous creatures

indicators.note: letters being distributed are spread about into a new order

parts.note: an ad is a short, little form of advertisement

explanation.surface: A small advert bans any praise, though the animals in it are beautiful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being distributed' mixes AD with FORBIDS and PRAISE together.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds of paradise are brilliantly plumed birds of New Guinea, famously gorgeous creatures.

clue.text: One who sounds like an almost identical person

definitions.meaning: a person who sounds bells in a church tower
a dead ... is someone who looks just like another

explanation.definitionFit: A bell-ringer sounds bells, and a 'dead ringer' is a near double of somebody else.

clue.text: Built battlements and was responsible for a production with a king's friend in it

indicators.note: in it means these pieces go inside the word for producing

parts.note: to have created something is to have been responsible for producing it
Nell Gwyn was the mistress of King Charles II

explanation.surface: Someone built castle walls and also staged a show with a royal companion in the cast.
explanation.walkthrough: NELL Gwyn, actress and favourite of Charles II, plus A go inside CREATED.
explanation.definitionFit: To crenellate is to furnish a wall with battlements, so crenellated means built with battlements.

clue.text: Replacing the first-class sound of what happens at Wimbledon

parts.note: super is an informal word for first-class

indicators.note: the sound of means the word for seeding players is taken as it is heard, not as spelt

parts.note: top tennis players are seeded, ranked so they avoid each other early in the tournament

explanation.surface: Something first-rate is replacing the familiar noises of the Wimbledon tennis tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: Wimbledon is the British tennis championship, famous for seeding its players; SEDING is spelt the way SEEDING sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To supersede something is to take its place, so superseding means replacing it.

clue.text: Woman who needs a penny to make a trick.

indicators.note: she needs the coin added, so the trick is the word with the penny letter taken away

parts.note: a fraud is a deceitful trick
D was the abbreviation for an old British penny

explanation.surface: A woman who must find a penny before she can perform a trick.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards: the woman plus D (old penny, from Latin denarius) makes FRAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: Frau is the German word for a woman or wife.

clue.text: Demeanor at the dance as a means of reducing friction

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
one's bearing is one's demeanour or deportment

explanation.surface: How someone carries themselves at a dance, oddly described as a way to cut friction.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings are small steel spheres in a race that let parts turn with little friction.

clue.text: Formerly single and about to start courting

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the word for single goes around the letter

parts.note: one means single

indicators.note: to start points at the opening letter of courting

explanation.surface: A person who was single and is just about to begin dating.
explanation.definitionFit: Once means at one time in the past, which is what formerly means.

clue.text: A branch of zoology is a girl's favourite science

parts.note: her is the possessive for a girl
a pet is a favourite
an ology is a jocular word for any science

explanation.surface: A girl's best-loved subject happens to be a branch of zoology.
explanation.definitionFit: Herpetology is the study of reptiles and amphibians, a field within zoology.

clue.text: Living together makes one study the young in one's advanced years

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart
a cub is a young animal
age means old age, advanced years

explanation.surface: Someone takes up studying young people in old age.
explanation.definitionFit: Concubinage is cohabitation of a couple without marriage.

clue.text: Seeds are scattered -by doctor but put in a row

indicators.note: seeds that are scattered are strewn about in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A doctor sows seeds at random but then plants them in a neat line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'are scattered' turns SEEDS into ESSED, placed by DR. Soldiers 'dress' ranks by aligning them.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops are dressed when lined up straight, so dressed means arranged in a line.

clue.text: Lots of water makes one pull in a climbing race

indicators.note: in puts the word for pull inside
in a down entry climbing means read upwards, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: seed means offspring or descendants, a race or line
to lug is to pull or haul

explanation.surface: Plenty of water lets a competitor drag something up in an uphill race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns SEED into DEES, and 'in' puts LUG inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge is a great flood, so deluges are large quantities of water.

clue.text: Study on gallery with teeth

parts.note: a den is a private study
the Tate is a London art gallery

explanation.surface: A study placed above an art gallery, somehow equipped with teeth.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' puts DEN above TATE; the Tate is a famous London gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: Dentate is a botanical and zoological term meaning toothed.

clue.text: Eats off the land

parts.note: reads like living on food gathered from the countryside, but describes the sea or weather wearing the ground away

explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away of soil and rock, which eats into the land.

clue.text: States in a genuine document

parts.note: real means genuine
MS is the abbreviation for manuscript, a document

explanation.surface: Something stated in an authentic paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Realms are kingdoms, that is, states.

clue.text: Accredit and support scrambled communication

indicators.note: scrambled means the letters of both words are jumbled together

explanation.surface: An instruction to authorise and back a coded message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scrambled' mixes ACCREDIT and SUPPORT; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A picture postcard is a card sent through the post, a form of written message.

clue.text: Panel doctors may prescribe it

definitions.meaning: a flat slab or plaque bearing an inscription

explanation.definitionFit: A tablet is both an inscribed slab and a pill, the sort of thing on a prescription.

clue.text: Exists among people as a religious belief

indicators.note: among means placed in the middle of the word for people

parts.note: them refers to people in general
is means exists

explanation.surface: Faith that exists among the population as a religious creed.
explanation.definitionFit: Theism is belief in a god or gods.

clue.text: Scattered when a means of communication goes back in all directions

indicators.note: in places the turned letters inside the compass points

parts.note: the four compass points south, east, west and north

indicators.note: goes back means the abbreviation is read from right to left

parts.note: R/T stands for radio telephony, a way of communicating

explanation.surface: Things lie scattered when a message travels back out every way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' turns RT into TR, which goes 'in' S, E, W, N.
explanation.definitionFit: Strewn means spread untidily over an area, i.e. scattered.

clue.text: Calls from the bush outside the window

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken from inside the run of clue words

explanation.surface: Cries coming from the shrubbery beyond the window.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is in 'buSH OUTSide'; 'the window' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Shouts are loud cries, which is one meaning of calls.

clue.text: A female holds a race to provide cover

indicators.note: holds means the pronoun contains the word for race

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a heat is a qualifying race

explanation.surface: A woman stages a race in order to offer shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: To sheathe something is to encase it, giving it a protective cover.

clue.text: Relationship of a novice with writing material

parts.note: L stands for learner, a novice, as on British learner plates
ink is used for writing

explanation.surface: A beginner's connection with pen and paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A link is a connection or bond between things, a relationship.

clue.text: Shock when the crazy turn up

indicators.note: in a down entry turn up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: nuts means crazy people

explanation.surface: A jolt when the madmen arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to shock or stupefy.

clue.text: Child who is born an animal

parts.note: a rat is an animal

explanation.surface: A child born a beast.
explanation.definitionFit: A brat is an ill-behaved child.

clue.text: I go off pop among the rifles adapted for adventurers

indicators.note: among means the other pieces sit in the middle of the jumbled word
adapted means the letters of rifles are altered into a new order

parts.note: to go pop, burst, is to go bust

explanation.surface: Someone bursting a balloon among guns reworked for soldiers of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapted' turns RIFLES into FILERS, and I plus BUST go 'among' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Filibusters were freebooters, irregular adventurers raiding Spanish America.

clue.text: It is the opposite of a joke to be senile

indicators.note: the opposite of means the phrase is read the other way round

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: Being senile is no laughing matter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga is informal for doddering or in one's dotage.

clue.text: I get married without someone to copy

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the word for marry wraps around

parts.note: to mate is to pair up or wed
a person is someone

explanation.surface: I wed with no one else involved, purely to imitate somebody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' in its old sense of outside puts MATE around PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: To impersonate is to imitate someone, to copy them.
